Foreign key linking to process.process_flow. Business justification: Capability indices are computed for parameters within a specific process flow. This FK enables process flow-level capability reporting and yield optimization analysis.

Foreign key linking to process.process_technology_node. Business justification: Capability indices are technology-node specific. Linking to process_technology_node enables node-level capability benchmarking and qualification tracking.

Foreign key linking to process.spc_control_chart. Business justification: Capability indices are derived from SPC control chart data. Linking capability to the source SPC chart enables traceability from capability analysis back to the underlying measurement history.
Foreign key linking to process.process_process_flow. Business justification: Change notifications affect a specific process flow; an internal FK provides direct reference within the process domain.

Foreign key linking to process.process_qualification. Business justification: Process changes often trigger re-qualification. This FK links the change notification to the associated qualification record.

Foreign key linking to process.process_step. Business justification: Process Change Notifications (PCNs) affect specific process steps. This FK links the PCN to the affected step, enabling step-level change impact analysis.

Foreign key linking to process.process_technology_node. Business justification: PCNs are associated with specific technology nodes. This FK links the change notification to the affected technology node.
Coolant flow rate in liters per minute.
Whether coolant is recirculated to reduce waste.
Percentage of coolant reclaimed/recycled.
Volume of coolant waste generated.
Duration of the cooling stage.
Energy consumed by the cooling process.
Cooling medium used (e.g., DI water, helium backside, chilled nitrogen).
Cooling method applied (e.g., convective, conductive, cryogenic, water-cooled chuck).
Whether cooling optimization is enabled for this step/recipe.
Cooling optimization option selected (e.g., energy_min, throughput_max, balanced).
Indicates whether this step/recipe includes a cooling process stage.
Controlled cooling ramp-down rate.
Target wafer/chamber temperature after cooling.
Foreign key linking to process.process_flow. Business justification: CMP conditions are defined within a specific process flow context. This FK links the condition to the process flow it supports.

Foreign key linking to process.process_step. Business justification: CMP conditions apply to specific CMP process steps. This FK links the condition to the step where it is used, enabling step-level condition management.
Foreign key linking to process.recipe. Business justification: CMP conditions are implemented via equipment recipes. This FK links the CMP condition to the specific recipe that implements it.
Waste elimination strategy (e.g., heat_recovery, coolant_reclaim, lean_idle_shutdown).
Whether waste heat is recovered/reused.
Automated or manual action triggered when the cooling condition falls outside its control limits. Defines the response protocol for out-of-spec cooling events.
Required ambient temperature in degrees Celsius within the process module or mini-environment during the cooling step. Ensures environmental control for sensitive process nodes.
Date on which this cooling condition was formally approved by the responsible engineer or process owner for production deployment.
Full name of the process or quality engineer who formally approved this cooling condition for production use. PII — masked in non-production environments.
Process chamber pressure in Torr during the cooling step. Vacuum or controlled-atmosphere conditions affect the cooling rate and prevent contamination.
Narrative description of the reason for creating or modifying this cooling condition. Supports process change management and audit trail requirements.
Set-point temperature of the electrostatic or mechanical chuck in degrees Celsius during the cooling step. Controls wafer backside heat transfer and uniformity.
ISO cleanroom classification required for performing this cooling step. Ensures the cooling environment meets contamination control requirements for the target technology node.

Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this cooling condition within the process engineering system. Used as a human-readable reference across process flows, equipment recipes, and qualification documents.
Detailed narrative description of the cooling condition, including its purpose within the process flow, applicable process steps, and any special handling notes.
Descriptive name for the cooling condition (e.g., 'Post-Etch Rapid Cool', 'Diffusion Furnace Ramp-Down'). Used in process documentation, traveler sheets, and operator interfaces.

Classification of the cooling method applied. Determines the thermal profile and equipment configuration required. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: rapid_cool|slow_cool|controlled_ramp|natural_convection|forced_convection|cryogenic — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]
Nominal flow rate of the cooling medium in standard liters per minute (SLM). Directly impacts cooling efficiency and uniformity across the wafer surface.
The cooling medium used to achieve the required thermal profile (e.g., nitrogen purge, forced air, helium backside cooling, chilled water). Determines equipment compatibility and safety requirements.
Pressure of the cooling medium in Torr, particularly relevant for helium backside cooling in vacuum process chambers. Affects thermal conductance between wafer and chuck.
Primary key for cooling_condition
Maximum allowable cooling duration in seconds before the wafer is flagged for review. Exceeding this limit may indicate equipment degradation or abnormal thermal load.
Nominal duration in seconds for the cooling step to reach the target temperature. Used for cycle time planning and equipment scheduling.
The nominal rate at which temperature is reduced, expressed in degrees Celsius per minute. Controls thermal stress on the wafer and prevents crystal defects or film delamination.
Maximum allowable cooling rate in degrees Celsius per minute. Exceeding this rate risks thermal shock, wafer warpage, or film stress failures.

Minimum acceptable process capability index (Cpk) for this cooling condition. Typically ≥1.33 for production qualification. Used to assess whether the cooling process is capable of meeting specification limits.
Timestamp when this cooling condition record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
Self-referencing FK on cooling_condition (derived_from_cooling_condition_id)
Date from which this cooling condition becomes effective in production process flows. May differ from approval date if a staged rollout is planned.
Type of semiconductor processing equipment for which this cooling condition is defined (e.g., diffusion furnace, RTP system, etch chamber, CVD reactor, track system). Ensures recipe compatibility.
Maximum allowable relative humidity percentage in the cooling environment. Excessive humidity can cause condensation on cooled wafers, leading to defects.
Indicates whether this cooling condition is currently active and available for use in process recipes. Inactive conditions are retained for historical traceability but cannot be assigned to new lots.
Indicates whether this is the default cooling condition for the associated process step and technology node. Used by recipe management systems to auto-assign conditions when no override is specified.
Method used to measure wafer or chuck temperature during the cooling step (e.g., thermocouple, pyrometer, RTD, infrared sensor). Determines measurement accuracy and calibration requirements.
Location on the wafer or equipment where the temperature is measured to determine cooling completion (e.g., wafer center, wafer edge, chuck surface, ambient).
Date on which this cooling condition was or will be retired from active use. Retained for historical traceability and audit purposes.
Full name of the process engineer responsible for defining, maintaining, and qualifying this cooling condition. PII — masked in non-production environments per VREQ-050.
Maximum allowable airborne particle count per cubic meter during the cooling step. Exceeding this limit may cause wafer contamination and yield loss.
Reference number of the Process Change Notification (PCN) that introduced or last modified this cooling condition. Links to the formal change management record.

The semiconductor manufacturing process step to which this cooling condition applies (e.g., photolithography, etch, diffusion, implant, deposition, metrology). Aligns the cooling condition to the correct process module.
Date on which this cooling condition was formally qualified for production use. Marks the start of the valid production window.
Current qualification status of this cooling condition for production use. Only 'qualified' conditions may be used in production process flows; others require engineering approval.
Version identifier of the process recipe in which this cooling condition is embedded. Supports recipe change management and traceability to qualification data.
Date by which this cooling condition must be requalified to remain valid for production use. Driven by process change notification (PCN) schedules or periodic review cycles.
Indicates whether a safety interlock must be engaged during this cooling step (e.g., chamber door lock, gas flow interlock). Ensures compliance with fab safety protocols.
Code identifying the originating process engineering or manufacturing execution system (MES) from which this cooling condition record was sourced (e.g., Camstar, WorkStream, Promis).
Type of SPC control chart applied to monitor this cooling condition in production. Determines the statistical method used to detect process drift or out-of-control conditions.
Required dwell time in seconds after reaching the target temperature to ensure thermal equilibrium before the wafer is transferred to the next process step.
The nominal target temperature in degrees Celsius to which the wafer or substrate must be cooled before proceeding to the next process step. Critical for thermal budget management.
The semiconductor technology node (e.g., 28nm, 14nm, 7nm, 5nm) for which this cooling condition is qualified. Ensures process compatibility with the target device geometry.
Lower control limit for the cooling endpoint temperature in degrees Celsius. Wafers below this limit may indicate over-cooling, which can cause condensation or thermal stress defects.
Upper control limit for the cooling endpoint temperature in degrees Celsius. Wafers exceeding this limit must be re-cooled or placed on hold per SPC rules.
Integrated thermal budget for the cooling step expressed in degree-Celsius-seconds (°C·s). Used to track cumulative thermal exposure and ensure device junction integrity.
Maximum allowable temperature non-uniformity across the wafer surface at the end of the cooling step, expressed as a percentage. Critical for within-wafer process uniformity and yield.
Timestamp of the most recent modification to this cooling condition record. Used for change tracking, SPC monitoring, and data freshness validation.
Substrate material for which this cooling condition is applicable. Different materials have distinct thermal conductivity and expansion coefficients requiring tailored cooling profiles.
Nominal wafer diameter in millimeters for which this cooling condition is defined (e.g., 200, 300, 450). Cooling parameters are wafer-size-dependent due to thermal mass differences.

Pressure of the backside cooling gas applied between the wafer and chuck, measured in Torr. Optimizing backside gas pressure improves wafer-to-chuck thermal conductance and wafer temperature uniformity.

Type of gas used for backside wafer cooling (typically helium) to enhance thermal contact between the wafer and chuck. Backside gas pressure and type are critical parameters in electrostatic chuck cooling optimization.

Wafer temperature measured under the pre-optimization (baseline) cooling configuration, in degrees Celsius. Provides the reference point against which optimization improvements are measured.
Iteration number within this run that yielded the optimal cooling performance result as defined by the optimization objective. Used to trace back to the specific parameter set that should be adopted.
Measured actual temperature of the chuck during the cooling optimization run, in degrees Celsius. Deviation from setpoint indicates cooling system performance and is a key optimization metric.

Target temperature setpoint for the electrostatic or mechanical chuck that holds the wafer during processing, in degrees Celsius. Chuck temperature directly controls wafer thermal uniformity and process outcomes.

Volumetric flow rate of the coolant during the optimization run, measured in liters per minute (LPM). A primary optimization variable controlling heat removal capacity from the process chamber or chuck.
Temperature of the coolant at the inlet to the cooling system during the run, measured in degrees Celsius. A key optimization parameter that sets the baseline thermal boundary condition.
Temperature of the coolant at the outlet of the cooling system during the run, measured in degrees Celsius. The delta between inlet and outlet temperatures quantifies heat absorbed from the process.
Operating pressure of the coolant circuit during the cooling optimization run, measured in kilopascals (kPa). Pressure affects flow rate, heat transfer efficiency, and system integrity.

Type of cooling medium used in the optimization run (e.g., deionized water, perfluorocarbon fluid, chilled water, nitrogen gas, helium gas). Determines heat transfer characteristics and compatibility with process chemistry.

Ratio of useful heat removed to total energy input for the cooling system during the run, expressed as a percentage. Measures the thermodynamic efficiency of the cooling configuration and supports energy optimization.
Date and time when this cooling optimization run record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance purposes.

Measured defect density on wafers processed during the cooling optimization run, expressed as defects per square centimeter. Used to correlate cooling parameter changes with defect generation and process quality.

Name or identifier of the Design of Experiment (DOE) design matrix used for this cooling optimization run (e.g., Box-Behnken, Central Composite, L9 Taguchi). Applicable when run_type is design_of_experiment.
Reference to the process engineer responsible for designing, executing, and analyzing this cooling optimization run. Used for accountability, knowledge management, and escalation routing.

Total electrical energy consumed by the cooling system during the optimization run, measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh). Supports energy efficiency analysis and sustainability reporting for fab operations.
Manufacturer model designation of the process equipment used in the cooling optimization run (e.g., ASML NXT:2000i, Applied Materials Centura). Supports equipment-specific parameter benchmarking.

Designated fabrication bay or cleanroom area within the fab where the cooling optimization run is executed (e.g., Bay 3A, Litho Bay, Diffusion Area). Used for spatial traceability and equipment grouping.
Reference to the specific process equipment unit on which the cooling optimization run is conducted. Links to the equipment master for tool specifications and maintenance history.
Reference to the wafer lot processed during the cooling optimization run. Enables correlation of cooling parameters with lot-level yield and electrical performance outcomes.

Rate at which heat is removed from the process chamber or wafer by the cooling system during the run, measured in Watts. Quantifies the effective cooling capacity achieved under the optimized parameters.

Free-text engineering notes capturing observations, anomalies, equipment issues, or contextual information relevant to this cooling optimization run. Supports knowledge transfer and root cause analysis.

Total number of parameter configuration iterations executed within this cooling optimization run. Tracks the breadth of the parameter space explored and the computational/experimental effort expended.

Statistical or computational method used to explore and optimize the cooling parameter space in this run (e.g., Design of Experiment full factorial, response surface methodology, gradient descent). Determines the experimental design and analysis approach.
Primary engineering objective driving this cooling optimization run. Defines the optimization criterion used to evaluate parameter configurations and select the optimal cooling setup.

Quantitative score representing the degree of optimization achieved in this run relative to the defined objective function. Higher scores indicate better optimization outcomes; used to compare runs and track improvement over time.
Wafer temperature achieved under the optimized cooling configuration identified by this run, in degrees Celsius. Compared against baseline to quantify the thermal improvement delivered.
Full name of the process engineer who owns and is accountable for this cooling optimization run. PII-tagged per VREQ-050; must be masked in non-production environments.

Process capability index (Cpk) calculated for the primary cooling parameter (e.g., chuck temperature) during this run. Cpk >= 1.33 is typically required for production qualification; used to assess cooling process stability.

Operating pressure inside the process chamber during the cooling optimization run, measured in millitorr (mTorr). Chamber pressure influences plasma density, etch/deposition rates, and thermal coupling.

Reference to the technology development or product program under which this cooling optimization run is conducted. Enables program-level aggregation of cooling optimization activities and resource tracking.

Radio frequency (RF) power applied to the process chamber during the run, measured in Watts. RF power is a primary heat source in plasma processes and directly determines the cooling load that must be managed.
Total elapsed time of the cooling optimization run from start to end, measured in minutes. Used for equipment scheduling, throughput analysis, and cycle time optimization.

Measured thermal resistance of the cooling interface between the chuck and the wafer, expressed in degrees Celsius per Watt (°C/W). Lower values indicate more efficient heat transfer and are a key optimization target.
Time required for the cooling system to reach thermal steady state at the target setpoint, measured in seconds. A key optimization metric; shorter stabilization times improve equipment throughput.
Date and time when this cooling optimization run record was last modified. Audit trail field supporting change tracking, data lineage, and incremental ETL processing.
Number of wafers included in the cooling optimization run. Determines thermal load and is used to validate cooling capacity under production-representative conditions.
Diameter of the wafers processed in this cooling optimization run, expressed in millimeters (e.g., 200, 300, 450). Wafer size directly impacts thermal mass and cooling system design requirements.

Measured peak-to-valley temperature variation across the wafer surface during the run, in degrees Celsius. A primary optimization objective; lower values indicate better thermal uniformity and improved process uniformity.

Estimated or measured change in wafer yield attributable to the cooling optimization, expressed as a percentage. Positive values indicate yield improvement; used to justify cooling optimization investments.

Automated or manual action triggered when the cooling condition falls outside its control limits. Defines the response protocol for out-of-spec cooling events.

Date on which this cooling condition was formally approved by the responsible engineer or process owner for production deployment.
Full name of the process or quality engineer who formally approved this cooling condition for production use. PII — masked in non-production environments.
Process chamber pressure in Torr during the cooling step. Vacuum or controlled-atmosphere conditions affect the cooling rate and prevent contamination.
Narrative description of the reason for creating or modifying this cooling condition. Supports process change management and audit trail requirements.
Set-point temperature of the electrostatic or mechanical chuck in degrees Celsius during the cooling step. Controls wafer backside heat transfer and uniformity.
ISO cleanroom classification required for performing this cooling step. Ensures the cooling environment meets contamination control requirements for the target technology node.

Externally-known alphanumeric code uniquely identifying this cooling condition within the process engineering system. Used as a human-readable reference across process flows, equipment recipes, and qualification documents.
Detailed narrative description of the cooling condition, including its purpose within the process flow, applicable process steps, and any special handling notes.
Descriptive name for the cooling condition (e.g., 'Post-Etch Rapid Cool', 'Diffusion Furnace Ramp-Down'). Used in process documentation, traveler sheets, and operator interfaces.

Classification of the cooling method applied. Determines the thermal profile and equipment configuration required. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: rapid_cool|slow_cool|controlled_ramp|natural_convection|forced_convection|cryogenic — promote to reference product if additional types are needed]
Nominal flow rate of the cooling medium in standard liters per minute (SLM). Directly impacts cooling efficiency and uniformity across the wafer surface.
The cooling medium used to achieve the required thermal profile (e.g., nitrogen purge, forced air, helium backside cooling, chilled water). Determines equipment compatibility and safety requirements.
Pressure of the cooling medium in Torr, particularly relevant for helium backside cooling in vacuum process chambers. Affects thermal conductance between wafer and chuck.
Primary key for cooling_condition
Maximum allowable cooling duration in seconds before the wafer is flagged for review. Exceeding this limit may indicate equipment degradation or abnormal thermal load.
Nominal duration in seconds for the cooling step to reach the target temperature. Used for cycle time planning and equipment scheduling.
The nominal rate at which temperature is reduced, expressed in degrees Celsius per minute. Controls thermal stress on the wafer and prevents crystal defects or film delamination.
Maximum allowable cooling rate in degrees Celsius per minute. Exceeding this rate risks thermal shock, wafer warpage, or film stress failures.

Minimum acceptable process capability index (Cpk) for this cooling condition. Typically ≥1.33 for production qualification. Used to assess whether the cooling process is capable of meeting specification limits.
Timestamp when this cooling condition record was first created in the system. Used for audit trail and data lineage tracking.
Self-referencing FK on cooling_condition (derived_from_cooling_condition_id)
Date from which this cooling condition becomes effective in production process flows. May differ from approval date if a staged rollout is planned.
Type of semiconductor processing equipment for which this cooling condition is defined (e.g., diffusion furnace, RTP system, etch chamber, CVD reactor, track system). Ensures recipe compatibility.
Maximum allowable relative humidity percentage in the cooling environment. Excessive humidity can cause condensation on cooled wafers, leading to defects.
Indicates whether this cooling condition is currently active and available for use in process recipes. Inactive conditions are retained for historical traceability but cannot be assigned to new lots.
Indicates whether this is the default cooling condition for the associated process step and technology node. Used by recipe management systems to auto-assign conditions when no override is specified.
Method used to measure wafer or chuck temperature during the cooling step (e.g., thermocouple, pyrometer, RTD, infrared sensor). Determines measurement accuracy and calibration requirements.
Location on the wafer or equipment where the temperature is measured to determine cooling completion (e.g., wafer center, wafer edge, chuck surface, ambient).
Date on which this cooling condition was or will be retired from active use. Retained for historical traceability and audit purposes.
Full name of the process engineer responsible for defining, maintaining, and qualifying this cooling condition. PII — masked in non-production environments per VREQ-050.
Maximum allowable airborne particle count per cubic meter during the cooling step. Exceeding this limit may cause wafer contamination and yield loss.
Reference number of the Process Change Notification (PCN) that introduced or last modified this cooling condition. Links to the formal change management record.

The semiconductor manufacturing process step to which this cooling condition applies (e.g., photolithography, etch, diffusion, implant, deposition, metrology). Aligns the cooling condition to the correct process module.
Date on which this cooling condition was formally qualified for production use. Marks the start of the valid production window.
Current qualification status of this cooling condition for production use. Only 'qualified' conditions may be used in production process flows; others require engineering approval.
Version identifier of the process recipe in which this cooling condition is embedded. Supports recipe change management and traceability to qualification data.
Date by which this cooling condition must be requalified to remain valid for production use. Driven by process change notification (PCN) schedules or periodic review cycles.
Indicates whether a safety interlock must be engaged during this cooling step (e.g., chamber door lock, gas flow interlock). Ensures compliance with fab safety protocols.
Code identifying the originating process engineering or manufacturing execution system (MES) from which this cooling condition record was sourced (e.g., Camstar, WorkStream, Promis).
Type of SPC control chart applied to monitor this cooling condition in production. Determines the statistical method used to detect process drift or out-of-control conditions.
Required dwell time in seconds after reaching the target temperature to ensure thermal equilibrium before the wafer is transferred to the next process step.
The nominal target temperature in degrees Celsius to which the wafer or substrate must be cooled before proceeding to the next process step. Critical for thermal budget management.
The semiconductor technology node (e.g., 28nm, 14nm, 7nm, 5nm) for which this cooling condition is qualified. Ensures process compatibility with the target device geometry.
Lower control limit for the cooling endpoint temperature in degrees Celsius. Wafers below this limit may indicate over-cooling, which can cause condensation or thermal stress defects.
Upper control limit for the cooling endpoint temperature in degrees Celsius. Wafers exceeding this limit must be re-cooled or placed on hold per SPC rules.
Integrated thermal budget for the cooling step expressed in degree-Celsius-seconds (°C·s). Used to track cumulative thermal exposure and ensure device junction integrity.
Maximum allowable temperature non-uniformity across the wafer surface at the end of the cooling step, expressed as a percentage. Critical for within-wafer process uniformity and yield.
Timestamp of the most recent modification to this cooling condition record. Used for change tracking, SPC monitoring, and data freshness validation.
Substrate material for which this cooling condition is applicable. Different materials have distinct thermal conductivity and expansion coefficients requiring tailored cooling profiles.
Nominal wafer diameter in millimeters for which this cooling condition is defined (e.g., 200, 300, 450). Cooling parameters are wafer-size-dependent due to thermal mass differences.

Pressure of the backside cooling gas applied between the wafer and chuck, measured in Torr. Optimizing backside gas pressure improves wafer-to-chuck thermal conductance and wafer temperature uniformity.

Type of gas used for backside wafer cooling (typically helium) to enhance thermal contact between the wafer and chuck. Backside gas pressure and type are critical parameters in electrostatic chuck cooling optimization.

Wafer temperature measured under the pre-optimization (baseline) cooling configuration, in degrees Celsius. Provides the reference point against which optimization improvements are measured.
Iteration number within this run that yielded the optimal cooling performance result as defined by the optimization objective. Used to trace back to the specific parameter set that should be adopted.
Measured actual temperature of the chuck during the cooling optimization run, in degrees Celsius. Deviation from setpoint indicates cooling system performance and is a key optimization metric.

Target temperature setpoint for the electrostatic or mechanical chuck that holds the wafer during processing, in degrees Celsius. Chuck temperature directly controls wafer thermal uniformity and process outcomes.

Volumetric flow rate of the coolant during the optimization run, measured in liters per minute (LPM). A primary optimization variable controlling heat removal capacity from the process chamber or chuck.
Temperature of the coolant at the inlet to the cooling system during the run, measured in degrees Celsius. A key optimization parameter that sets the baseline thermal boundary condition.
Temperature of the coolant at the outlet of the cooling system during the run, measured in degrees Celsius. The delta between inlet and outlet temperatures quantifies heat absorbed from the process.
Operating pressure of the coolant circuit during the cooling optimization run, measured in kilopascals (kPa). Pressure affects flow rate, heat transfer efficiency, and system integrity.

Type of cooling medium used in the optimization run (e.g., deionized water, perfluorocarbon fluid, chilled water, nitrogen gas, helium gas). Determines heat transfer characteristics and compatibility with process chemistry.

Foreign key linking to process.cooling_process. Business justification: Cooling optimization runs are conducted to optimize a specific cooling process. This FK links the optimization run to the cooling process being optimized.

Ratio of useful heat removed to total energy input for the cooling system during the run, expressed as a percentage. Measures the thermodynamic efficiency of the cooling configuration and supports energy optimization.
Date and time when this cooling optimization run record was first created in the system. Audit trail field for data lineage and compliance purposes.

Measured defect density on wafers processed during the cooling optimization run, expressed as defects per square centimeter. Used to correlate cooling parameter changes with defect generation and process quality.

Name or identifier of the Design of Experiment (DOE) design matrix used for this cooling optimization run (e.g., Box-Behnken, Central Composite, L9 Taguchi). Applicable when run_type is design_of_experiment.
Reference to the process engineer responsible for designing, executing, and analyzing this cooling optimization run. Used for accountability, knowledge management, and escalation routing.

Total electrical energy consumed by the cooling system during the optimization run, measured in kilowatt-hours (kWh). Supports energy efficiency analysis and sustainability reporting for fab operations.
Manufacturer model designation of the process equipment used in the cooling optimization run (e.g., ASML NXT:2000i, Applied Materials Centura). Supports equipment-specific parameter benchmarking.

Designated fabrication bay or cleanroom area within the fab where the cooling optimization run is executed (e.g., Bay 3A, Litho Bay, Diffusion Area). Used for spatial traceability and equipment grouping.
Reference to the specific process equipment unit on which the cooling optimization run is conducted. Links to the equipment master for tool specifications and maintenance history.
Reference to the wafer lot processed during the cooling optimization run. Enables correlation of cooling parameters with lot-level yield and electrical performance outcomes.

Rate at which heat is removed from the process chamber or wafer by the cooling system during the run, measured in Watts. Quantifies the effective cooling capacity achieved under the optimized parameters.

Free-text engineering notes capturing observations, anomalies, equipment issues, or contextual information relevant to this cooling optimization run. Supports knowledge transfer and root cause analysis.

Total number of parameter configuration iterations executed within this cooling optimization run. Tracks the breadth of the parameter space explored and the computational/experimental effort expended.

Statistical or computational method used to explore and optimize the cooling parameter space in this run (e.g., Design of Experiment full factorial, response surface methodology, gradient descent). Determines the experimental design and analysis approach.
Primary engineering objective driving this cooling optimization run. Defines the optimization criterion used to evaluate parameter configurations and select the optimal cooling setup.

Quantitative score representing the degree of optimization achieved in this run relative to the defined objective function. Higher scores indicate better optimization outcomes; used to compare runs and track improvement over time.
Wafer temperature achieved under the optimized cooling configuration identified by this run, in degrees Celsius. Compared against baseline to quantify the thermal improvement delivered.
Full name of the process engineer who owns and is accountable for this cooling optimization run. PII-tagged per VREQ-050; must be masked in non-production environments.

Process capability index (Cpk) calculated for the primary cooling parameter (e.g., chuck temperature) during this run. Cpk >= 1.33 is typically required for production qualification; used to assess cooling process stability.

Operating pressure inside the process chamber during the cooling optimization run, measured in millitorr (mTorr). Chamber pressure influences plasma density, etch/deposition rates, and thermal coupling.

Foreign key linking to process.process_flow. Business justification: Cooling optimization runs are conducted within a specific process flow context. This FK links the optimization run to the process flow it supports.

Foreign key linking to process.process_step. Business justification: Cooling optimization runs are conducted for a specific process step. This FK links the optimization run to the step being optimized.

Indicates whether the optimized cooling parameters identified in this run are recommended for adoption in production process recipes. True = parameters approved for production use; False = further optimization or validation required.

Reference to the technology development or product program under which this cooling optimization run is conducted. Enables program-level aggregation of cooling optimization activities and resource tracking.

Radio frequency (RF) power applied to the process chamber during the run, measured in Watts. RF power is a primary heat source in plasma processes and directly determines the cooling load that must be managed.
Total elapsed time of the cooling optimization run from start to end, measured in minutes. Used for equipment scheduling, throughput analysis, and cycle time optimization.
Date and time when the cooling optimization run was completed or terminated. Used with run_start_timestamp to calculate total run duration and equipment utilization.

Classification of the cooling optimization run by its engineering purpose: baseline characterization, parametric sweep across cooling variables, design of experiment (DOE), validation of optimized parameters, or production monitoring run.

Indicates whether the cooling process parameters were within Statistical Process Control (SPC) control limits throughout the optimization run. True = all parameters in control; False = one or more SPC violations detected.

Semiconductor technology node (process generation) for which this cooling optimization run is performed, expressed in nanometers (e.g., 7nm, 5nm, 3nm). Determines thermal budget constraints and cooling requirements.

Reduction in wafer temperature achieved by the optimized cooling configuration compared to baseline, in degrees Celsius (baseline_wafer_temp_c minus optimized_wafer_temp_c). Key performance indicator for the optimization run.

Measured thermal resistance of the cooling interface between the chuck and the wafer, expressed in degrees Celsius per Watt (°C/W). Lower values indicate more efficient heat transfer and are a key optimization target.
Time required for the cooling system to reach thermal steady state at the target setpoint, measured in seconds. A key optimization metric; shorter stabilization times improve equipment throughput.
Date and time when this cooling optimization run record was last modified. Audit trail field supporting change tracking, data lineage, and incremental ETL processing.
Number of wafers included in the cooling optimization run. Determines thermal load and is used to validate cooling capacity under production-representative conditions.
Diameter of the wafers processed in this cooling optimization run, expressed in millimeters (e.g., 200, 300, 450). Wafer size directly impacts thermal mass and cooling system design requirements.

Measured peak-to-valley temperature variation across the wafer surface during the run, in degrees Celsius. A primary optimization objective; lower values indicate better thermal uniformity and improved process uniformity.

Estimated or measured change in wafer yield attributable to the cooling optimization, expressed as a percentage. Positive values indicate yield improvement; used to justify cooling optimization investments.
Pressure of the backside cooling gas in Torr. Controls thermal coupling between the wafer and the electrostatic chuck or susceptor during cooling.

Process chamber pressure in millitorr during the cooling step. Relevant for vacuum-based cooling processes where heat transfer is pressure-dependent.

became.before: Unified record tracking the full design-in lifecycle from initial registration through confirmed design-win for semiconductor products selected by customers. became.before: Transactional record documenting the Known Good Die (KGD) certification status for die bank inventory. became.before: Association record capturing parent-child relationships between wafer lots, die banks, and finished goods to enable full forward and backward traceability across split, merge, rework, retest, and packaging transformations. Supports IATF 16949 traceability, automotive PPAP documentation, customer complaint root cause analysis, and field return investigation.

Supports technology roadmap execution tracking and CHIPS Act program reporting.

affected_objects.before: Reference master for semiconductor process technology nodes and generations (e.g., 28nm, 16nm FinFET, 7nm EUV, 3nm GAA, 2nm CFET). SSOT for technology node classification used across design, fabrication, and research domains.

became.before: Master record for individual audit findings and their full Corrective/Preventive Action (CAPA) lifecycle raised during compliance audit events, regulatory inspections, customer complaints, or internal compliance assessments. Captures finding reference, parent audit event, finding type (major/minor nonconformance, observation, OFI), clause violated, finding description, source event type.
